chunks: 5416 - Al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir narrated from Abān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever does not make his bequest properly at the time of death, that is a deficiency in his dignity and his intellect."

And he said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم made a will to ‘Alī عليه السلام, and ‘Alī made a will to al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥasan عليه السلام made a will to al-Ḥusayn, and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام made a will to ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام made a will to Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī al-Bāqir عليه السلام."

key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ٱلْبَاقِرِ: Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī al-Bāqir عليه السلام, named here in the line of وصية
key_terms.نَقْصًا فِي مُرُوءَتِهِ: a deficiency in his dignity and manly virtue
key_terms.وَصِيَّتَهُ: his bequest or will made at death

ai.seo_question: Why is making a proper bequest before death considered important in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that making a proper bequest at the time of death is a mark of dignity and sound intellect. It also situates وصية within the transmitted practice of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, linking it to the succession of authority from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم through the Imams عليهم السلام.
